core_obligations: One direction (proof lines 10004-10005): a finite etale morphism is locally a disjoint union of isomorphisms, so the sheaf it represents is finite locally constant.
Produce local representatives (proof lines 10005-10008): if the sheaf is finite locally constant, an etale covering trivializes it and gives finite etale morphisms representing the restrictions.

Descend (proof lines 10008-10018): arguing as in the cited descent result, the local representatives carry a descent datum for schemes, which is effective, and the resulting morphism is finite etale by the descent results for those properties.
proof_roadmap: Show that represented sheaves are finite locally constant using the local structure of finite etale morphisms.
Trivialize a finite locally constant sheaf over an etale covering to obtain local representatives.
Build the descent datum by copying the standard construction and descend it to obtain the representing finite etale scheme.
difficulty_reason: The lemma characterizes finite locally constant sheaves of sets on the small etale site as exactly those represented by finite etale schemes (statement lines 9993-10001). The proof is a complete argument in both directions: one direction follows from the local structure of finite etale morphisms (proof lines 10004-10005); conversely a finite locally constant sheaf is trivialized over an etale covering, the local representing objects are shown to carry a descent datum by the same construction as in the cited descent lemma (proof lines 10005-10008), and effectivity together with the descent results for finiteness and etaleness produces the desired morphism (proof lines 10008-10018). The non-formal content is the descent step and the transfer of the two properties. The claim is H2: a two-direction argument with every descent input named.
